newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK AVG CPI INFLATION SEEN AT 8.3PCT IN 96-MIN.
newsitem.headline: GREEK AVG CPI INFLATION SEEN AT 8.3PCT IN 96-MIN.

text.p: Greek National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou said the average CPI inflation will fall to 8.3 percent in 1996 from 9.3 percent in 1995 and the average rate on the marker 12-month T-bill to 12.7 percent from 15.5 percent last year.

Real GDP growth will accelerate to 2.6 percent in 1996 from 2.0 percent in 1995 and the public sector budget deficit will be slashed to 7.6 percent of GDP from 9.0 percent in 1995, Papandoniou told reporters.
The average wage for workers rose by six percent in real terms in the period 1994-1996, he added.
"To conclude, in nominal convergence terms, Greece has covered about two thirds of the distance that separated her from the Maastricht Treaty criteria in 1993," said Papandoniou.
Papandoniou went over the structural measures taken by the socialist administration in the period 1994-96 and blasted the conservative party for disputing the successes of the socialist government.
Greece is holding early elections on September 22 and the two main political parties have started exchanging fire over the economy. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
